position_in_era.primary_genre_lineage: flamenco × copla × jazz × soul (translation across diaspora)
position_in_era.geographic_locus: Palma de Mallorca (Buika's home) / Madrid (recording, with Javier Limón producing)
position_in_era.historical_role: Born in Palma de Mallorca to Equatorial-Guinean Bubi parents, Buika translates *between* Black diaspora vocal traditions (jazz, soul, Black Cuban) and Andalusian copla / flamenco — sometimes within a single phrase. *Mi Niña Lola* (2006), produced by Javier Limón (the same producer who made *Lágrimas Negras*), is her flamenco-zambra-as-jazz-diva statement; uDiscover and AllMusic both treat her as a defining post-Camarón translator on the female-voice axis.

narrative_slots.production_facts: Released 3 April 2006 on DRO Atlantic. Produced by Javier Limón. Sold 80,000+ copies in Spain; strong sales in France.
narrative_slots.member_dynamics: Born 11 May 1972, Palma de Mallorca, to parents from Equatorial Guinea (Bubi ethnic group). Producer Javier Limón links her work directly to the *Lágrimas Negras* / Cigala–Bebo flamenco–Cuban translation circuit.
narrative_slots.cultural_venue: Palma de Mallorca / Madrid. Later cinematic visibility through Pedro Almodóvar's *La piel que habito* (2011) soundtrack.
narrative_slots.instrumentation_details: Voice (Buika) over flamenco guitar plus jazz piano, upright bass, percussion. The album emphasises copla and zambra-style flamenco.
narrative_slots.release_circumstances: Re-introduced *Mi Niña Lola* (the title track, originally recorded ~50 years prior). Latin Grammy nominee.
